adelaide-1.name: Adelaide Botanic Garden
adelaide-1.bio: Free garden at the east end of North Terrace, open daily, with large lawns and a museum of economic botany.

adelaide-2.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (single source; resolve-pin LOW, OSM rate-limited)

adelaide-3.name: Art Gallery of South Australia
adelaide-3.bio: Free state art gallery on North Terrace, with Australian, Aboriginal and European collections.
adelaide-3.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (single source; resolve-pin LOW, OSM rate-limited)

adelaide-4.name: South Australian Museum
adelaide-4.bio: Free state museum on North Terrace, with natural history galleries and an Aboriginal cultural collection.
adelaide-4.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates, within 12 m of the Wikivoyage listing point and 41 m of the Commons photo median (two sources agree)
adelaide-4.notes: Free per southaustralia.com listing and Wikivoyage; open daily 10am-5pm per the museum site.

adelaide-5.name: Glenelg
adelaide-5.bio: Beachside suburb reached by tram from the city, with a long jetty, Moseley Square and a sandy beach.
adelaide-5.coordinates_source: Wikipedia article coordinates (Moseley Square/jetty end); Commons photo median is 160 m west on the sand (resolve-pin LOW)

adelaide-7.name: Adelaide Zoo

adelaide-7.notes: Adult $49.50 from zoossa.com.au; keeper talks free. Giant pandas per the zoo's own and SATC listings.

destination.name: Adelaide
destination.tagline: A park-ringed capital with free museums, a tram to the beach and wine close by.
destination.description: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia, set on a plain between the Adelaide Hills and Gulf St Vincent. Colonel William Light laid it out as a grid of wide streets surrounded by parklands, and the plan largely survives. North Terrace holds the state museum, art gallery and botanic garden, while the Central Market and Rundle Mall sit a few blocks south. Famous wine regions, including the Barossa, McLaren Vale and the Adelaide Hills, border the city.
whyVisit: Ride the tram to the beach

goodToKnow.title: Free central trams
goodToKnow.detail: Tram travel between the Entertainment Centre, Botanic Garden and South Terrace is free, and so are the City Connector buses.

goodToKnow.title: Summer heat waves
goodToKnow.detail: Several heat waves a year push temperatures above 40 °C, so keep walks and zoo visits to the morning.

goodToKnow.title: Festival season rush
goodToKnow.detail: Arts, music and sport festivals fill mid-February to late March, so book beds and tickets early.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are mild, and March brings the Fringe and Festival season.
